items.followUp: Name two raw materials required for photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis requires light energy and chlorophyll to absorb it.
rubric.description: Names light or chlorophyll as a necessary condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either valid condition.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide and water are the raw materials used to make glucose.
rubric.description: Names carbon dioxide or water as a necessary condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either valid condition.

modelAnswer: Two necessary conditions for photosynthesis are sunlight and chlorophyll.
Other necessary conditions include carbon dioxide and water.

rubric.why: Bioenergetics concerns energy in living organisms.
rubric.description: Identifies the subject as the study of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the study of energy.

rubric.why: The subject is energy transformations in living organisms.
rubric.description: Links energy transformations to living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning living organisms or energy transformations.

modelAnswer: Bioenergetics is the study of energy transformations in living organisms.

items.followUp: Name two food sources of vitamin A.

rubric.why: These are examples of foods that provide vitamin C.
rubric.description: Names one fruit or other food source of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid source.

rubric.why: A second valid food source is required for the question.
rubric.description: Names another source of vitamin C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid source.

modelAnswer: Sources of vitamin C include citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons, guava, tomatoes, and green vegetables.
Any two of these are sufficient.

items.followUp: State one function of dietary fibre in the human digestive system.

rubric.why: Dietary fibre consists mainly of indigestible plant material such as cellulose.
rubric.description: Identifies fibre as indigestible plant material or cellulose.

rubric.why: Fibre adds bulk to food and helps its movement through the gut.
rubric.description: States that fibre adds bulk or helps bowel movement/prevents constipation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct function.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibres are indigestible parts of plant foods, such as cellulose.
They add bulk to food and help its movement through the digestive tract.

items.followUp: What causes marasmus, and name one of its symptoms.

rubric.why: Kwashiorkor is caused mainly by an inadequate protein intake, often after weaning.
rubric.description: States the dietary cause of Kwashiorkor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying protein deficiency or inadequate protein in the diet.

rubric.why: These are characteristic symptoms of Kwashiorkor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid symptom.

modelAnswer: Kwashiorkor is caused mainly by a severe deficiency of protein in the diet, often after a child is weaned.
Symptoms include edema (swelling), a swollen abdomen, stunted growth, and changes in hair or skin.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a macronutrient and a micronutrient.

rubric.why: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts; carbohydrates, proteins and fats are examples.
rubric.description: States the large requirement for macronutrients or gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or a correct example.

rubric.why: Micronutrients are needed in small amounts; vitamins and minerals are examples.
rubric.description: States the small requirement for micronutrients or gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or a correct example.

modelAnswer: Macronutrients are nutrients required by the body in large amounts, such as carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
Micronutrients are nutrients required in small amounts, such as vitamins and minerals.

items.followUp: How does wind speed affect the rate of transpiration?

rubric.why: A rise in temperature generally increases water evaporation and transpiration.
rubric.description: States that higher temperature increases the rate of transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of effect.

rubric.why: Heat speeds evaporation of water from leaf surfaces, raising transpiration.
rubric.description: Gives the reason for the increase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking temperature to faster evaporation or water loss.

modelAnswer: As temperature rises, the rate of transpiration generally increases.
Higher temperature speeds the evaporation of water from leaf surfaces.

items.followUp: Trace the path of blood in systemic circulation.

rubric.why: Pulmonary circulation begins when blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
rubric.description: Gives the route of blood from the heart to the lungs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the right ventricle and pulmonary artery route.

rubric.why: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs to the heart through pulmonary veins and enters the left atrium.
rubric.description: Gives the return route from the lungs to the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the pulmonary veins and left atrium route.

modelAnswer: In pulmonary circulation, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs through the pulmonary veins and enters the left atrium.
